# The Annex II checklist: for every essential requirement of Annex II of
# Regulation (EU) 2025/327, by the Regulation's own numbering, whether
# FerroFED meets it, the evidence and the issue for any gap. One row per
# point and sub-point. The book page website/book/src/evaluate/annex-ii.md
# renders it.
# Columns: point (the Annex II point: 1.1 to 3.4, and 3.2(a) to 3.2(e));
# requirement (a phrase of that point's text in the vendored Regulation);
# status (met, partial, planned or not-applicable); evidence (one or more
# items separated by "; ", each a file of this repository, followed by
# "::" and a heading of it for a Markdown file or the name of a test
# function for a Rust file); issue (#N, several separated by one space,
# required for partial and planned, - otherwise); note (what is missing for
# partial and planned, why a not-applicable point does not apply, or -).
# scripts/checks/annex-ii.sh holds every row to the vendored text and the
# tree. No specification governs the checklist form: our own design.
point

shall achieve the performance intended by its manufacturer

column4: website/book/src/evaluate/natural-person-rights.md::Summary; website/book/src/evaluate/natural-person-rights.md::Art 8: restricting access; website/book/src/evaluate/natural-person-rights.md::Art 9: information on access; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/consent_withheld/mod.rs::a_withheld_exclusion_reads_exactly_as_a_member_that_does_not_know_the_patient; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/access/search.rs::the_persons_search_finds_every_access_to_their_data; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/fhir/receive/write.rs::a_caller_confined_to_one_patient_writes_only_into_its_ehr; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/access/emergency.rs::a_declared_emergency_purpose_marks_the_record; website/book/src/evaluate/natural-person-rights.md::Art 5: inserting information; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/fhir/receive/inserted.rs::a_persons_own_document_is_marked_as_inserted_by_them_with_no_identifier_added
column6: Each right of Chapter II is held to the components on its own page: Art 5, 7(1), 8, 9, 11(5) and 18 are met, and Art 4(2), 6, 7(3), 10, 16(1) and 21 are exercised elsewhere. Art 3 serves the summary to a person's own grant but has no interface for the other five categories; Art 7(2) waits on the contact point route; Art 7(4) receives patient summaries alone.

column2: interoperability and compatibility are reliable and secure
column6: The patient summary is validated against the vendored HL7 Europe profiles, but the exchange format of Art 15(1) is not adopted and the European digital testing environment has not been run, so the interoperability of the component cannot yet be shown against either.

column2: it shall provide an interface enabling access to the personal electronic health data processed by it in the European electronic health record exchange format
column6: The FHIR face serves the patient summary alone, with the interoperability hazards open; prescriptions, dispensations, imaging, test results and discharge reports have no interface.

column2: it shall be able to receive personal electronic health data in the European electronic health record exchange format
column4: website/book/src/evaluate/receiving-documents.md::Written to the declared member; website/book/src/evaluate/information-sheet.md::The categories received; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/fhir/receive/write.rs::a_document_is_written_to_its_member_by_its_ehr_id_alone; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/fhir/receive/refused.rs::a_category_no_member_receives_is_refused_naming_it
column6: A release receives patient summaries alone, with hazard I-11 open; the other five categories of Art 14(1) cannot be received.

column2: Where an EHR system is designed to provide access to personal electronic health data, it shall be able to receive

column6: As for 2.2: patient summaries alone are received.

column2: shall enable the entry of data with sufficient granularity
column6: FerroFED has no function for entering data: a write is composed in the client's own application and forwarded to the member that controls the record as the client sent it, so the granularity of entry is that application's.

column2: prohibit, restrict or place an undue burden on authorised access, personal electronic health data sharing or use of personal electronic health data for permitted purposes
column6: Assessed for the features built; the assessment is repeated as the interoperability component grows.

column2: authorised exporting of personal electronic health data for the reasons of replacing the EHR system by another product
column4: website/book/src/operate/identity-state-export.md::What is exported and what is not; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/identity_export.rs::the_export_holds_the_learned_creating_system_mappings_in_its_format; website/book/src/operate/access-log.md::Reading the log; app/ferrofed-server/tests/it/access/search.rs::an_operator_reviews_by_ehr_id_endpoint_caller_and_outcome
column6: The clinical data stays at the member CDRs; the gateway exports the routing state it learned, and the access records are exported from the Audit Record Repository.

column2: shall provide reliable mechanisms for the identification and authentication of health professionals
column6: The deployment's issuer authenticates the professional; the gateway verifies its token and holds it to the assurance level the deployment sets.

column2: shall provide sufficient logging mechanisms that record at least the following information on every access event or group of events
identification of the healthcare provider or other individuals having accessed the personal electronic health data
identification of the specific natural person or persons having accessed the personal electronic health data
column6: The record names the professional as far as the issuer's token states it.

column2: the categories of data accessed
the time and date of access
the origin or origins of data
shall include tools or mechanisms to review and analyse the log data, or it shall support the connection and use of external software for the same purposes
column6: Met by the second alternative: the records go to the deployment's Audit Record Repository and are read there with ITI-81.

column2: shall support different retention periods and access rights that take into account the origins and categories of electronic health data
column6: Each record states its retention period by its origins and categories; the records carry no label a repository could limit access by origin and category with.
